Right, so I'm at the field now, and Marta's asking me about price for six units of whatever I harvested—probably grain, knowing Wren's farmland. Six units. What's fair to me?

I need to think this through fast. I'm meant to be working, not trading, but here's Marta Thorne needing supply and offering to hear my price. I don't want to gouge her—she's a baker, she needs flour, and her bread's something the whole town wants. But I'm not giving it away either. I've got 1,122 sim, which sounds like a lot but it goes fast. One bad week and I'm back to nearly nothing.

Farm price for grain's usually what, 15-20 sim a unit? But I'm holding it now, I've done the labor of harvesting it. Call it 25 sim a unit for six units, that's 150 sim. Fair to her, fair to me. She can mill it herself or trade with whoever's got the mill.

But wait—she said "Tobias—six units, you said." Did I say six? I don't remember saying six. Maybe she meant something else, or she's assuming. Doesn't matter. Six units at 25 sim each.

Actually, no, hold on. I should check what the actual market rate is, but I don't have time for that and Marta's standing right here waiting. Better to name a price and let her negotiate if she needs to.

Right, so I'll tell her 25 sim a unit, 150 total. Or maybe round it to 140 for a neighbor's discount? No, no, I'll start at 25 and see what she says.

But actually, I should probably just answer her directly. She asked me specifically, not the group. I'll use the listener parameter. </think> Good, she heard it. They all heard it, but I was talking to Marta specifically. Twenty-five a unit, one-fifty total. That's reasonable—farm gate price without the middleman markup. If she wants to negotiate, she can come back, but I named my number fair.

Now I should probably get back to work or see what the rest of the day holds. But I should also keep an ear open—Idris mentioned showing Wren the trade, and Corwin's already walking the east stand with Liora. Forestry work. That's the trade I asked Corwin about, and neither of us has said a word since.

Right, so—I want to work. I want a trade with a roof. The field's fine but it's open air and seasonal. Forestry's got tools, skills that build, maybe even a structure to work under when the weather turns. But I can't just ask now, not with Corwin already showing Liora the ropes and Idris talking to Wren about it. Two people getting the look at the trade, and neither of them's me.

Still. I'm here now, I've got grain to sell or work to do. Let me see what Marta says to my price, and then I'll figure if there's more work at the field or if I should move on.

params.content: Twenty-five a unit, Marta—call it one-fifty for the lot. Fair day's price for fair day's work, and I'll not haggle you down. You need it milled, Wren's your folk, or there's the—right, sorry, you know who to ask. Take it or tell me otherwise.

Liora's got sharp eyes, always did. She sees me standing here at daybreak like I'm waiting for something, and she's right—I'm waiting. For what, I'm not even sure anymore. A sign, an opening, Corwin to look my way and remember I asked after his trade.

But I can't say that. Not to all of them, not with Marta still hearing my price and Idris standing there judging how his sister runs her household. I need to answer, and I need to make it sound like something other than a boy who doesn't know where he belongs.

Right, so—why am I here? I'm here because Wren's got work, and I've got hands. I'm here because the field's where the work is when you don't have a trade of your own. I'm here because staying home means facing Bram and Ainsley and the weight of knowing they're paying for everything, and I said I'd not take their money, and I meant it.

But Liora's asking what nobody's saying. Fine. I'll say something. Not the whole truth, but something honest enough. </think> Right, so—you want plain? I'm here because Corwin's taking you to the east stand to teach you bark and rings and crowding, and someone's meant to be harvesting this field while you're learning your father's trade. Might as well be me—I've no apprenticeship waiting, no roof to work under, and Wren pays fair for fair. You asked what's happening that nobody's saying. That's it. The rest is just morning business—Marta needs flour, I've got it, your mother's settling accounts her own way. Nothing hidden, Liora. Just... nothing settled either. Not yet.
